content.title:
Daniel Lurie on Instagram: "Vanderbilt University—one of the great research universities in the world—has chosen San Francisco as the home for a full-time academic campus.

Beginning in 2027, @vanderbiltu plans to bring students, faculty, and all the energy that comes with academic life into the heart of our city.

If we want San Francisco to lead the future, we must compete for the institutions that shape it.

As part of Vanderbilt University’s plan to establish a presence in San Francisco, Vanderbilt and the California College of the Arts have agreed that Vanderbilt will acquire CCA’s campus after the wind down of CCA’s operations in 2027.
 
CCA has been part of San Francisco’s cultural and creative fabric for more than a century.
 
I appreciate Vanderbilt’s commitment to preserving CCA’s archives, supporting alumni engagement, and continuing the Wattis Institute of Contemporary Arts as part of a new CCA Institute at Vanderbilt.

Today shows what happens when we stay focused, work together, and aim high.

San Francisco is on the rise.

And we’re just getting started."

CCA has been part of San Francisco’s cultural and creative fabric for more than a century. I appreciate Vanderbilt’s commitment to preserving CCA’s archives, supporting alumni engagement, and continuing the Wattis Institute of Contemporary Arts as part of a new CCA Institute at Vanderbilt.Today shows what happens when we stay focused, work together, and aim high.San Francisco is on the rise.And we’re just getting started.This CCA grad and onetime faculty has zero time for your tone deaf video. Apparently the arts are fine for you to have as background for your ego, but David Huffman and countless faculty & staff are losing their jobs - not to mention the creative brain drain that is happening in SF as artists flee technocrats and an unfathomable cost of living.Today was actually pretty devastating for those of us at CCA, which you failed to even mention. Our school has been a pillar of the arts in the bay area for 119 years, this is a huge loss for the art and design community. Not to mention all the students and staff whose educations and livelihoods are being uprooted. We aren’t celebratingCool painting, bro. Sure hope the artist who goes uncredited in this video doesn’t have an extensive legacy connected to this institution that you also do not name or a whole community of students, artists, and SF residents (ie voters) that you also clearly do not care aboutThe tone deaf nature of your announcement @danielluriesf in this is absolutely appalling. No amount of comments below it will make up for what you did not say at first, since most people will not even read them. To not even recognize or acknowledge that the loss of the third art school in the region and the second in SF that has brought so much to the bay area and SF over the last century, shows you have no real respect or interest for the arts in this city. And worst yet, you celebrate the upcoming death of CCA and the arrival of Vanderbilt University in front of a painting by black artist Davis Huffman, a current CCA faculty member, who was just told he’s losing his job!CCA faculty member here. I voted for you, had a house party for you, and supported a lot of your initiatives concerning housing. Today is not a day to celebrate. What about the faculty and staff jobs being LOST? CCA was the last real arts education institution in the Bay Area. I’ve been proud to be part of the CCA community and its absence will leave a void.CCA student here: they blindsided us and we have no viable options especially the international students like meClosing CCA is a terrible loss for the Bay Area arts community.You’re ridiculous. This is a tragedy for arts education in San Francisco. Not to mention all the faculty, students, and staff caught up in this mess.You don’t deserve that David Huffman. You need to actually get out in the city. The Arts have always been a crucial part of SF and the Bay Area. Your ignorance to what is actually happening is deafening. Enjoy your robots. 🤖 that’s all that will be left.Can we get a video of you mentioning that we lost an institution that can’t be replaced and was also the birthplace and home of the Arts & Crafts movement. CCA contributed to the true creative culture of San Francisco and attracted students from all over the world including this brown kid. 💔✊🏽💔WHATEVER!!! What about the young students who were meant to their education there, how dishonest and corrupt to take their money when the school knew they had other plans! With SFAI gone and now CCA there is nothing left to draw and keep artists in San Francisco. A stain on the soul and future of this city!bit hypocritical, lurie to not mention cca with a david huffman piece sitting right behind you? dill-weed.insane to frame the closure of a 119 year old bay area institution this wayYou are losing an incredible arts community, closing cca is a huge loss for the Bay Area.
